In [[abstract algebra]], a '''dialgebra''' is the generalization of both [[algebra]] and [[coalgebra]]. The notion was originally introduced by Lambek as "subequalizers",<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Lambek | first = Joachim
 | doi = 10.4153/CMB-1970-065-6
 | journal = [[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]]
 | mr = 274552
 | pages = 337–349
 | title = Subequalizers
 | volume = 13
 | year = 1970| issue = 3
 }}</ref><ref name=bh/> and named as dialgebras by Tatsuya Hagino.<ref>{{cite conference
 | last = Hagino | first = Tatsuya
 | editor1-last = Pitt | editor1-first = David H.
 | editor2-last = Poigné | editor2-first = Axel
 | editor3-last = Rydeheard | editor3-first = David E.
 | contribution = A typed lambda calculus with categorical type constructors
 | doi = 10.1007/3-540-18508-9_24
 | pages = 140–157
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = [[Lecture Notes in Computer Science]]
 | title = Category Theory and Computer Science, Edinburgh, UK, September 7–9, 1987, Proceedings
 | volume = 283
 | year = 1987| isbn = 978-3-540-18508-6
 }}</ref><ref name=bh>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Backhouse | first1 = Roland
 | last2 = Hoogendijk | first2 = Paul
 | doi = 10.1051/ita:1999126
 | issue = 4–5
 | journal = RAIRO Theoretical Informatics and Applications
 | mr = 1748664
 | pages = 401–426
 | title = Final dialgebras: from categories to allegories
 | url = https://www.numdam.org/article/ITA_1999__33_4-5_401_0.pdf
 | volume = 33
 | year = 1999}}</ref> Many algebraic notions have previously been generalized to dialgebras.<ref>{{cite conference
 | last1 = Poll | first1 = Erik
 | last2 = Zwanenburg | first2 = Jan
 | editor1-last = Corradini | editor1-first = Andrea
 | editor2-last = Lenisa | editor2-first = Marina
 | editor3-last = Montanari | editor3-first = Ugo
 | contribution = From algebras and coalgebras to dialgebras
 | contribution-url = https://www.cs.ru.nl/E.Poll/papers/cmcs01.pdf
 | doi = 10.1016/S1571-0661(04)80915-0
 | edition = 1
 | pages = 289–307
 | publisher = Elsevier
 | series = [[Electronic Notes in Theoretical Computer Science]]
 | title = Coalgebraic Methods in Computer Science, CMCS 2001, a Satellite Event of ETAPS 2001, Genova, Italy, April 6–7, 2001
 | volume = 44
 | year = 2001| hdl = 2066/19049
 | hdl-access = free
 }}</ref> Dialgebra also attempts to obtain [[Lie algebra]]s from associated algebras.<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Loday | first = Jean-Louis
 | editor1-last = Loday | editor1-first = Jean-Louis
 | editor2-last = Chapoton | editor2-first = Frédéric
 | editor3-last = Frabetti | editor3-first = Alessandra
 | editor4-last = Goichot | editor4-first = François
 | contribution = Dialgebras
 | doi = 10.1007/3-540-45328-8_2
 | isbn = 3-540-42194-7
 | mr = 1860994
 | pages = 7–66
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = [[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]]
 | title = Dialgebras and Related Operads
 | volume = 1763
 | year = 2001
 | zbl = 0999.17002}}</ref>
